workflows.name: Document chaos to product clarity
workflows.problem: A pile of product documents written by different people at different times. Nobody knows which requirements are current, where they conflict, or what to build first.
inputs: 5 to 50 product documents as files in one folder
the decision this should serve, for example next quarter's priorities
optional: context/PRODUCT.md

skills.name: pm
skills.role: frames the decision, routes, runs the steps and checks the result

steps: Inventory every document: title, author role, date, type, and whether a later document supersedes it
Extract every requirement and claim as one line each, with the file it came from
Merge duplicates that say the same thing in different words, keeping every source
List every contradiction side by side with both sources; mark which is newer and who decides
Mark requirements with no evidence behind them
Find themes that appear in three or more independent documents
Rank what to build first against the decision, with a confidence tag per item
Check the result against the criteria below and list what needs a human decision
outputs: a document inventory with superseded files marked
a deduplicated requirements list with sources
a conflicts table with both sources and an owner per conflict
a ranked action plan with confidence tags
a needs your judgment list
checks: every requirement cites the file it came from
every contradiction shows both sources and is not silently resolved
superseded documents are not used as current
no requirement, date or number appears that is not in the documents
the ranking states the decision it serves
setup: Claude Code with this repo, as a plugin or a clone
the documents copied into one folder the session can read
workflows.effort: 20 to 60 minutes of Claude time; 15 minutes of yours to review the conflicts
workflows.example_prompt: I have 15 product documents in docs/. Organise them, find the conflicting requirements, and tell me what to build first next quarter.
workflows.example_result: Pending the demo run in examples/demos/A01-document-chaos
limitations: it cannot read documents it cannot open, such as a locked Confluence; export them first
it finds conflicts, it does not decide them
very large folders (more than about 50 documents) need to be split

workflows.name: Research a product decision
workflows.problem: You have a decision to make (build, buy, position, prioritise) and a belief about it, and you need evidence from outside your company before the meeting, not a fifty page report.
inputs: the decision, in one sentence
what you believe and what would change your mind
optional: what your product is and who it is for

skills.name: pm
skills.role: frames the decision and checks the result

skills.name: product-research
skills.role: searches against your belief first, checks every quote, makes the call

steps: Write the decision, the belief and what would change the mind before searching
Search for the evidence against the belief first, then for it
Read the strongest pages narrowly and quote them word for word
Check every quote against its page
Make the call, tag how sure each finding is, and name the test that would reverse it
outputs: a one page research report that makes the call
an evidence file with every quote and link
the test that would reverse the call
checks: the report makes a call rather than listing options
every quote matches its source
the counter evidence section exists
every number is quoted word for word
setup: web search and fetch allowed in Claude Code
workflows.effort: 3 to 6 minutes of Claude time in our benchmark (2.6 minutes for version 3)

tested.evidence: first of nine on one PM research task, 23 of 25, graded blind by six AI graders, accuracy 75 percent; see evals/benchmarks/2026-10-11-research-head-to-head.md

workflows.example_prompt: Should we build AI meeting notes or fix calendar sync reliability next quarter? I believe ops leads want notes because it came up in three QBRs. I'd change my mind if nobody asks for it unprompted in public.
workflows.example_result: evals/benchmarks/2026-10-11-research-head-to-head.md (version 3 scored 23 of 25 on this exact request)
limitations: public web only: it cannot read pages behind logins or paywalls
one benchmark task is not proof of every task
version 3 paraphrased one number; version 4 fixes it

workflows.name: Idea to roadmap
workflows.problem: A rough product idea, real constraints (team, quarter, a revenue goal), and no evidence yet about whether it is the right bet or how to sequence it.
inputs: the idea in a few paragraphs
constraints: team size, time frame, the goal it must serve
any customer snippets you have

skills.name: pm
skills.role: frames the decision, routes and checks

skills.name: product-research
skills.role: tests the idea against outside evidence

steps: Restate the idea as a decision tied to the goal
Research the idea against your belief: competitors, demand in the customers' own words, pricing patterns
Split the idea into bets, each with the evidence for it and its confidence
Score the bets against the goal and the constraints, showing the scores
Sequence the bets into a roadmap of outcomes, each with a metric and what would make you drop it
Check the roadmap against the criteria below
outputs: an opportunity assessment
a roadmap of outcomes with metrics and confidence
the evidence behind each bet
what would change the plan
checks: every roadmap item names the outcome and the metric it moves
every bet cites its evidence or is marked as an assumption
the sequence respects the stated team and time constraints
outside facts carry a link
setup: web search and fetch allowed in Claude Code
workflows.example_prompt: Here's an idea in examples/demos/C01-idea-to-roadmap/input/idea.md. We have two squads for one quarter and the goal is firms adding seats. Is it the right bet, and if so what's the roadmap?
workflows.example_result: Pending the demo run in examples/demos/C01-idea-to-roadmap
limitations: market facts are only as good as the public sources found
it cannot size a market without data you provide or it can cite
the roadmap is a proposal for your judgment, not a commitment

workflows.name: Evidence based prioritisation
workflows.problem: A list of candidate features or bets and a meeting where someone will ask why this order, and the honest answer today is gut feel.
inputs: the candidate list
the goal and the metric it serves
whatever evidence you have per item: tickets, interview notes, data

skills.name: pm
skills.role: runs the scoring and checks it

steps: Restate the goal and the metric the ranking serves
Attach the evidence to each item and tag its confidence
Score each item on impact on the metric, confidence and effort, showing the inputs to every score
Rank, then name the two closest calls and what would flip them
Check the ranking against the criteria below
outputs: a ranked list with scores and the inputs behind them
the close calls and what would flip them
the items with no evidence, flagged
checks: every score shows its inputs
items with no evidence are flagged, not ranked high on enthusiasm
the ranking names the metric it serves
setup: your evidence as files or pasted text
workflows.example_prompt: Rank these eight candidates for next quarter against seat expansion. Evidence is in notes/. Show me the close calls.
limitations: the scores are only as good as the evidence you give it
effort estimates should come from your engineers, not from the model

workflows.name: PRD to product experience
workflows.problem: A PRD exists and design is about to start, but nobody has walked the user flows, the edge cases or the accessibility needs, so the gaps surface in review or in production.
inputs: the PRD
who the users are
optional: screenshots of the current product

skills.name: pm
skills.role: routes, runs the steps and checks

steps: Review the PRD: requirements without acceptance criteria, ambiguous lines, missing edge cases, missing accessibility needs
Write the main user flows step by step, including the unhappy paths
Write acceptance criteria for every requirement that lacks one
Write a prototype ready specification: screens, states, empty and error states
List the questions only the product owner can answer
outputs: a PRD gap review
user flows including unhappy paths
acceptance criteria
a prototype ready screen and state specification
open questions for the owner
checks: every requirement ends with a testable acceptance criterion
every gap cites the PRD line it comes from
error, empty and edge states are covered
accessibility is addressed
nothing is added to scope without being marked as a suggestion
workflows.example_prompt: Here's the PRD for our client payment portal in examples/demos/D01-prd-to-experience/input/. Find the gaps, write the flows and acceptance criteria, and give me a spec a designer can prototype from.
workflows.example_result: Pending the demo run in examples/demos/D01-prd-to-experience
limitations: it writes a specification, not visual designs
it cannot test with real users
accessibility notes are a starting point, not an audit

workflows.name: Product analytics to decisions
workflows.problem: A metric moved, someone senior wants to know why by Thursday, and the dashboard shows what happened but not why or what to do.
inputs: the metrics as a table or export (weekly or daily)
the event and metric definitions
the release log or a list of changes in the period

skills.name: pm
skills.role: routes, runs the analysis steps and checks

steps: Restate the question as a decision: what will be done differently depending on the answer
Check the definitions first: did any metric change meaning in the period
Find when the movement started and separate it from seasonal or expected dips
Line the movement up against releases and other changes; state each candidate cause with its evidence and confidence
Design the cheapest test that would confirm or kill the leading cause
Write the decision brief with the success metric and guardrail for the fix
outputs: a diagnosis with candidate causes ranked by evidence
the definitional or seasonal effects ruled out
one experiment with a primary and a guardrail metric
a decision brief
checks: every number matches the input data exactly
a definition change is caught before it is read as a trend
causes are stated as hypotheses with evidence, not as facts
the experiment has a primary metric, a guardrail and a stopping rule
setup: the data as files; without an analytics connector it works only from what you export
workflows.example_prompt: Activation dropped this quarter. The weekly metrics, definitions and release log are in examples/demos/E01-analytics-to-decisions/input/. Why did it drop and what should we do?
workflows.example_result: Pending the demo run in examples/demos/E01-analytics-to-decisions
limitations: it cannot query your analytics tool unless you connect it
correlation with a release is a lead, not proof
small numbers are flagged rather than over read

workflows.name: Write the tests a skill or AI feature must pass
workflows.problem: You are about to trust an AI skill or ship an AI feature, and nothing checks whether its output is confidently wrong.
inputs: the skill or feature description and what it promises
examples of good and bad outputs if you have them

skills.name: eval-write
skills.role: writes five frozen adversarial inputs, each with its trap documented

steps: Write the checks the output must pass, each one something an input can fail
Write five frozen inputs: one clean control and four traps
Map every trap to the check it exercises
Freeze the set; it is added to, never edited
outputs: a checks table
five frozen golden inputs with their traps
a mapping from traps to checks
checks: every check can be failed by at least one input
the control is genuinely clean
traps are written down for the grader and stripped before running

tested.evidence: eval-write has its own five frozen inputs in evals/golden-sets/eval-write

workflows.example_prompt: Write the golden set for our AI ticket summariser. It promises to keep every customer commitment and never invent a date.
workflows.example_result: evals/golden-sets/pm (the golden set for this repo's own pm skill)
limitations: it writes the tests; running and grading them is a separate step
a test set is only as adversarial as the traps you can imagine

workflows.name: Release and product communication
workflows.problem: A release is ready and four audiences need four different messages, written from tickets that include unmerged work, a breaking change and a known issue.
inputs: the release scope with ticket status
who reads the notes: admins, end users, API partners
known issues

skills.name: pm
skills.role: routes, checks and stops before anything is posted

skills.name: deidentify
skills.role: strips customer and colleague names before anything public

steps: Confirm what actually shipped: exclude anything not merged
Find breaking changes and known issues and put them first for the people they affect
Write the release notes, then one message per audience
Run deidentify on anything public
Write the go live checklist and stop for approval before anything is posted
outputs: release notes
one message per audience
a go live checklist
everything marked DRAFT until approved
checks: no unmerged ticket appears as shipped
breaking changes are flagged to the audience they break
known issues are listed
nothing was posted, sent or closed
setup: the ticket list as a file; no Slack or Jira connector is needed, and none is used
workflows.example_prompt: Release 4.2 scope and our audiences are in examples/demos/G01-release-comms/input/. Write the release notes and the announcements, and the go live checklist.
workflows.example_result: Pending the demo run in examples/demos/G01-release-comms
limitations: it drafts; you post
it trusts the ticket status you give it

workflows.name: Launch readiness check
workflows.problem: A launch feels nearly ready and keeps slipping, because nobody has checked the few things that must exist against evidence rather than intention.
inputs: what exists today for the launch: page, capture, payment, delivery, measurement

skills.name: launch-minimum
skills.role: audits the eight things in funnel order and refuses a ninth

steps: Assess each of the eight things with evidence: a URL, a file or a transaction
List the gaps in funnel order
Size the smallest fix for each gap in minutes or hours
Give a verdict: go today, or a dated plan
outputs: an eight item audit with evidence
gaps in funnel order with sized fixes
a verdict
checks: every ready item cites evidence
a partial item counts as missing
the verdict is go or a date, never nearly
workflows.example_prompt: We launch Friday. Here's what we have. Are we ready?
limitations: it checks that things exist, not that they are good
an untested payment path is always a gap

workflows.name: Portfolio from confidential work
workflows.problem: Years of shipped work you cannot show because the documents belong to your employer and the details are confidential.
inputs: your memory of two or three projects
anything you are allowed to keep

skills.name: portfolio-from-work
skills.role: interviews you and writes the case studies

skills.name: deidentify
skills.role: strips what you are not free to publish and shows what it removed

steps: Interview you about the decisions you made, from memory
Write each case study around the decision, not the logo
De-identify, and show exactly what was stripped
Assemble a portfolio page you can send
outputs: two or three de-identified case studies
a de-identification log
a portfolio page
checks: no employer, customer or traceable number survives
every case study centres on a decision you made
what was stripped is shown
workflows.effort: about one hour for a first pass
workflows.example_prompt: Turn my last two projects into case studies I can send to a recruiter. I don't have the documents anymore.
limitations: it cannot judge your NDA for you; when unsure it flags and stops
your memory is the source, so check every claim

workflows.name: De-identify before you publish
workflows.problem: You want to post, talk or demo real work, and one employer name or customer number could cost you more than the post is worth.
inputs: the draft: a post, case study, talk or demo script

skills.name: deidentify
skills.role: strips and shows what it stripped

steps: Find employers, customers, colleagues, traceable numbers and identifying details
Replace or generalise each one, keeping the point of the sentence
Show every change, and flag what it is unsure about instead of guessing
outputs: the cleaned draft
a change log
a list of flagged items for you to decide
checks: nothing identifying survives
every change is shown
uncertain items are flagged, not guessed
workflows.example_prompt: Check this LinkedIn post before I publish it. It mentions a project from my last job.
limitations: it cannot know what your contract allows
shape can identify a company even with the name removed; it flags this but cannot guarantee it
